title: Lorenzo's French accent and Tio's own reluctant music study
summary: Lorenzo spoke and wrote French; Tio admits he was a wayward boy who loved horses and learned clarinet from his father, uncle and brother, plus some violin.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I know some people have told me that your brother seemed to have a French accent. I mean, certain people have told me how he would talk. They would start quoting, you know, saying certain things. And they would try to imitate a French accent. Do you remember? Did he have sort of a French?

Yes, he did, because I'll tell you why, because, you see, he was taught in French, in better words, he spoke French and English language. He spoke the French language frequently and he's read it. Also written it. He knew that because he learned that. Like I told you, I was kind of a little bad boy. I didn't, if they tried to catch me to do that, I was gone. Yeah, I didn't want to get part of that. I didn't, all I wanted to do, I love horses and I used to like to be around horses and I like to be doing something. Sometimes I was an animal, but I loved them. When it came to be confined to one thing only, I couldn't do it. I couldn't do it, I couldn't see myself doing it. That's the reason why I tell you, I learned music, I learned clarinet, I learned the violin from AJP. I didn't finish learning, but anyhow, I started with him. Carinet, I learned that with my father and my uncle and my brother. My brother was the last that I had dealing with. Brother, he couldn't do too much with me because I could run away from him. I would tell him what I wanted, see. I was a bad boy. Well, I'm sorry to take what, but not only that, but probably I would help somebody else, not myself, because for my part, it's all over. I love music very much. In better words, I really love opera. Boys turn on the radio and hear all that jazz and stuff.
